text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Pakistan Muslim League (PML) President Nawaz Sharif has said his party would form governments at the centre and in all the four provinces.

- The Pakistan People's Party (PPP) has decided to put up Makhdoom Amin Fahim as chief minister for the Sindh province if its efforts for the formation of a coalition government in Sindh succeed, Sindh PPP chief Qaim Ali Shah said.
- Elections against 46 seats of the Senate will be held in the first week of March.
- The government has lifted curfew from Khanewal town in Punjab which was imposed after clashes between Moslems and Christians.
- Three people have died and another was admitted to a hospital in Hyderabad city when they consumed poisonous liquor.
- President PML Nawaz Sharif will meet President Farooq Leghari today, party sources said.
- Gold prices have hit a five-month low in the last three weeks mainly on a surge in imports by the two recently authorised companies and the resumption of operation by ARY traders.

- Robust rally was witnessed on the Karachi Stock Exchange during pre-election and post-election sessions and the index scored over a century as market capitalisation rose by 27 billion rupees because of Nawaz Sharif's win in the elections.
